page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i3g.13xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 52 virtual CPUs across 26 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, paired with 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 3.69 GB of RAM per core. The instance includes 2879 GB of local SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 16 Gbps, operating under a KVM hypervisor.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by stress-ng single-core and single-threaded gzip compression tests, which fall into the bottom 25% tier. However, the high core count compensates in parallel workloads, with multi-core stress-ng, Geekbench multi-core, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression all achieving average tier results. Memory bandwidth tests, including both cached small-block and uncached large-block reads, also perform within the average range.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.i3g.13xlarge lies in its moderate single-core speed versus its high resource density. While individual core performance is limited, the instance offers qualitative cost efficiency for applications that can leverage parallel execution across its 52 vCPUs alongside its substantial 2879 GB local SSD storage. This makes it a balanced option for storage-heavy workloads that do not require top-tier single-thread compute speeds but benefit from localized high-capacity SSD storage.

Given these hardware and performance parameters, this instance is well-suited for database hosting, distributed file systems, static web serving, and moderate multi-threaded data processing. It is also capable of handling Redis key-value stores and medium-scale LLM inference tasks where parallel processing and local storage capacity are prioritized over raw single-core execution speed.
